% Display snippets for docs/clpq.md (Clausal Prolog). The program sections
% are tested by clpq_sig_tests.clausal; entailed_1 is the seam spelling.

% === Unified syntax ===

% --8<-- [start:int_int_produces_fraction]
X is 7 / 2         % 3.5 — evaluation: float division
X is 6 / 2         % 3.0
X is rdiv(7, 2)    % 7 rdiv 2 — exact
X is rdiv(6, 2)    % 3 — an integral quotient presents as an integer
X is 1 / 0         % raises error(evaluation_error(zero_divisor), (/)/2)
% --8<-- [end:int_int_produces_fraction]

% --8<-- [start:int_int_produces_fraction_ex2]
{X = 1/3}               % CLP(Q) constraint: X = 1 rdiv 3
{X = 6/2}               % X = 3 (an integer)
{X + Y = 1/2}           % CLP(Q) constraint, posted: X + Y = 1/2
{X = 1/3 + 1/3 + 1/3}   % X = 1, exactly
% --8<-- [end:int_int_produces_fraction_ex2]


% === Builtins ===

% --8<-- [start:rational_1]
rational(X)                    % X is rational, unbounded
rational([X, Y, Z])            % all three are rational
% --8<-- [end:rational_1]

% --8<-- [start:in_q_3]
in_q(X, 0, 10)                 % X in [0, 10]

% Equivalent to:
rational(X), {0 =< X, X =< 10}

% For lists, pass the list:
in_q([X, Y, Z], 0, 10)
% --8<-- [end:in_q_3]

% --8<-- [start:maximize_2_and_minimize_2]
% Classic linear program:
% maximize 30*X + 50*Y subject to:
%   2*X + Y =< 16
%   X + 2*Y =< 11
%   X + 3*Y =< 15
%   X, Y >= 0

lp(X, Y, OBJ) :-
    in_q([X, Y], 0, 1000),
    {2*X + Y =< 16, X + 2*Y =< 11, X + 3*Y =< 15},
    maximize(30*X + 50*Y, OBJ).
% -> X = 7, Y = 2, OBJ = 310  (all exact rationals, all bound)
% --8<-- [end:maximize_2_and_minimize_2]

% --8<-- [start:sup_2_and_inf_2]
bounds(X, LO, HI) :-
    in_q(X, 0, 100),
    {X =< 10, X >= 3},
    inf(X, LO),            % LO = 3
    sup(X, HI).            % HI = 10
% X remains unbound — only LO and HI are set
% --8<-- [end:sup_2_and_inf_2]

% --8<-- [start:entailed_1]
test_entailed(X) <- (
    in_q(X, 0, 100),
    X <= 4,
    entailed(X <= 5),          # true: X <= 4 implies X <= 5
    not entailed(X <= 3)       # false: X could be 4, which is > 3
)
% --8<-- [end:entailed_1]

% --8<-- [start:int_minimize_3]
% Minimum integer X such that X >= 3/2
int_min(X, COST) :-
    in_q(X, 0, 10),
    {X >= 3/2},
    int_minimize([X], X, COST).
% -> X = 2, COST = 2

% min(X) with X >= Y + Z, Y >= 2, Z >= 2, all integer
resource_min(X, Y, Z, COST) :-
    in_q([X, Y, Z], 0, 100),
    {X >= Y + Z, Y >= 2, Z >= 2},
    int_minimize([X, Y, Z], X, COST).
% -> X = 4, Y = 2, Z = 2, COST = 4
% --8<-- [end:int_minimize_3]

% --8<-- [start:dump_q_2]
show_constraints(X, Y, CS) :-
    in_q([X, Y], 0, 100),
    {2*X + Y =< 16, X + 2*Y =< 11},
    dump_q([X, Y], CS).
% CS = ['{_40 + 2*_41 =< 11}', '{2*_40 + _41 =< 16}', '{-_40 =< 0}', '{_40 =< 100}', ...]
% (a list of atoms; the variables print as _N names)
% --8<-- [end:dump_q_2]


% === Constraint examples ===

% --8<-- [start:linear_equalities]
% Two-variable system: X + Y = 10, X = 3 -> Y = 7
two_var(X, Y) :-
    in_q([X, Y], 0, 10),
    {X + Y = 10, X = 3}.
% -> X = 3, Y = 7  (exact)
% --8<-- [end:linear_equalities]

% --8<-- [start:linear_equalities_ex2]
% Three equations in three unknowns:
% X + Y + Z = 6, X - Y = 2, Y - Z = 1
three_var(X, Y, Z) :-
    in_q([X, Y, Z], -100, 100),
    {X + Y + Z = 6, X - Y = 2, Y - Z = 1}.
% -> X = 11 rdiv 3, Y = 5 rdiv 3, Z = 2 rdiv 3  (exact fractions)
% --8<-- [end:linear_equalities_ex2]

% --8<-- [start:linear_equalities_ex3]
% Rational coefficients: (1/2)*X + (1/3)*Y = 1, Y = 0
rational_coeffs(X, Y) :-
    in_q([X, Y], -10, 10),
    {1/2 * X + 1/3 * Y = 1, Y = 0}.
% -> X = 2, Y = 0
% --8<-- [end:linear_equalities_ex3]

% --8<-- [start:linear_inequalities]
% Feasibility: X + Y =< 8, X =< 5, Y =< 6
feasible(X, Y) :-
    in_q([X, Y], 0, 100),
    {X + Y =< 8, X =< 5, Y =< 6}.
% Succeeds — the feasible region is non-empty
% --8<-- [end:linear_inequalities]

% --8<-- [start:linear_inequalities_ex2]
% Infeasible: X >= 6 and X =< 4 is impossible
infeasible(X) :-
    in_q(X, 0, 10),
    {X >= 6, X =< 4}.
% Fails — no solution exists
% --8<-- [end:linear_inequalities_ex2]

% --8<-- [start:optimization]
% Minimize cost subject to resource constraints
scheduling(X, Y, COST) :-
    in_q([X, Y], 0, 100),
    {X + Y >= 10,          % need at least 10 total
     2*X + Y =< 30,        % resource constraint 1
     X + 3*Y =< 40},       % resource constraint 2
    minimize(5*X + 3*Y, COST).
% --8<-- [end:optimization]


% === Interaction with CLP(Z) and CLP(R) ===

% --8<-- [start:fd_q_coexistence]
% X is integer-constrained AND participates in a rational equation
mixed(X, Y) :-
    in_domain(X, 1, 10),        % CLP(Z): X in {1..10}
    in_q(Y, 0, 10),             % CLP(Q): Y in [0, 10]
    {X + Y = 10},               % CLP(Q)
    {Y = 7}.                    % -> X = 3 (integer, accepted by both FD and Q)
% --8<-- [end:fd_q_coexistence]

% --8<-- [start:dispatch_table]
lp(X, Y, OBJ) :-
    in_q([X, Y], 0, 1000),
    {2*X + Y =< 16, X + 2*Y =< 11, X + 3*Y =< 15},
    maximize(30*X + 50*Y, OBJ).
% -> X = 7, Y = 2, OBJ = 310
% --8<-- [end:dispatch_table]

% --8<-- [start:dispatch_table_ex2]
% First branch: X = 5.  Second branch: X = 3.
% Each branch sees only its own constraints.
choice(X) :-
    in_q(X, 0, 10),
    {X = 5}.
choice(X) :-
    in_q(X, 0, 10),
    {X = 3}.
% --8<-- [end:dispatch_table_ex2]
